title: How do you build a training matrix for a charity?
description: Build a charity training matrix: board duties, volunteers, child safety, screening, disability support, privacy and whistleblowing, with triggers and records.
shortAnswer: A charity training matrix is built by listing the board, paid staff, volunteers and contractors as separate rows, then switching on columns according to what the charity actually does: governance duties for every registered charity, child safety and screening where it works with children, disability support standards where it is a registered provider, and privacy, whistleblower and modern slavery measures where size thresholds are met. Each cell records the trigger, the interval and the evidence a regulator could request.
keyTakeaways: A charity's columns depend on its activities and size, not its sector label: child services, NDIS registration, revenue and employee numbers each switch obligations on or off.
Volunteers usually need rows of their own. Victoria's Child Safe Standard 8 covers staff and volunteers, and Working with Children Check rules distinguish employee and volunteer clearances.
The board is a training audience in its own right: ACNC Governance Standard 5 expects charities to bring Responsible Persons' duties to their attention and provide regular information or training.
Several charity duties are about screening or policy rather than courses, so the matrix should hold clearance checks and policy acknowledgments alongside training.
Regulators ask for evidence on request rather than routine filing: the ACNC needs no submission for the Governance Standards but expects evidence if asked.

sections.heading: What makes a charity's training obligations different from a company's?

blocks.text: A charity's obligations switch on according to what it does and how large it is, and much of its workforce is unpaid. Two charities registered with the same regulator can need very different matrices: one running a youth sports program needs child safety columns, while one providing disability supports needs NDIS columns.

The method in [how to build a training matrix](/guides/how-to-build-a-training-matrix) still applies. What a charity adds is an applicability step at the start: list each activity, each revenue or headcount threshold and each registration, and decide which columns apply before assigning any training. Recording that decision gives a reviewer the reason a column is absent as well as present, which matters when a charity grows past a threshold or starts a new program. A [compliance obligations register](/glossary/compliance-obligations-register) is a natural place to keep that decision.

sections.heading: Which people should a charity list as rows?

blocks.text: Separate the board, paid staff, volunteers and contractors, then split each by the activity they perform. Rules frequently name volunteers or board members explicitly, so merging them with employees hides duties.

sections.heading: Which obligations apply to charities, and when do they switch on?

blocks.text: Most of the columns below apply only if a condition is met. The summaries are drawn from the linked regulation pages; the core charity rules covered there are Australian, with EU rules noted for charities that operate in Europe.

items: **Every registered Australian charity (except Basic Religious Charities).** Section 45.25(2) of the ACNC Regulations 2022 requires reasonable steps to ensure Responsible Persons are subject to and comply with seven duties. The ACNC's suggested steps include letters of appointment, regular information or training, and acting when duties are not met ([ACNC Governance Standard 5](/regulations/acnc-governance-standards-board-duties)).

**Charities working with children in Victoria.** The sectors in Schedule 1 of the Child Wellbeing and Safety Act 2005 include charities that provide services for children. Child Safe Standard 8 requires staff and volunteers to receive ongoing education and training, starting with training on the Child Safety and Wellbeing Policy ([Victorian Child Safe Standards](/regulations/victoria-child-safe-standards-training)).

**Child related work in NSW, Victoria and Queensland.** A Working with Children Check is screening, not training. NSW employers verify each worker online and keep a record of each verification; Victorian organizations check that the worker has added the organization's name and should record number, expiry and card type; Queensland organizations link workers to a blue card account and keep a register ([Working with Children Checks](/regulations/working-with-children-check-requirements)).

**Registered NDIS providers.** Workers complete the mandatory Worker Orientation Module, receive infection prevention and control training with refreshers, and work within a training system that identifies mandatory training and evaluates its effectiveness ([NDIS worker training](/regulations/ndis-practice-standards-worker-training)).

**Charities that are public companies.** A whistleblower policy is required, and RG 270 expects training for every employee and specialist training for eligible recipients. ASIC gave relief from the policy requirement to not-for-profit companies limited by guarantee with revenue under $1 million ([whistleblower policy](/regulations/whistleblower-policy-training-requirements)).

**Charities with revenue of at least $100 million.** The Modern Slavery Act 2018 requires a statement describing actions to assess and address risks, and section 16 gives staff training as an example ([Modern Slavery Act](/regulations/modern-slavery-act-training)).

**Privacy.** The Privacy Act small business exemption ends at $3 million annual turnover, subject to listed exceptions; the OAIC lists regular staff training as an example of APP 1.2 practices ([Privacy Act](/regulations/privacy-act-staff-training-requirements)). Charities established in the EU fall under the GDPR, where the data protection officer monitors awareness raising and training under Article 39(1)(b) ([GDPR](/regulations/gdpr-staff-training-requirements)).

**EU charities with 50 or more workers.** The Whistleblower Directive requires internal reporting channels for private sector legal entities with 50 or more workers, and volunteers are among the people it protects when they report ([EU Whistleblower Directive](/regulations/eu-whistleblower-directive-obligations)).

sections.heading: Which charity training intervals are fixed and which are chosen?

blocks.text: Very few are fixed. Most charity rules require training to be ongoing, regular or appropriate, and leave the interval to the organization, so triggers matter more than calendar dates.

items: **Event triggers.** Victoria's guide expects induction before work with children begins and when roles change; NSW only allows workers with a status of Cleared or Application in progress to be engaged; NDIS orientation comes before supports are delivered.

**Screening expiry dates.** NDIS Worker Screening Checks are valid for up to 5 years, and NSW employers verify again after a five year WWCC renewal. These belong in the matrix as dated cells even though they are not courses.

**Chosen intervals.** Standard 8 indicators expect policy training at induction and at regular intervals; the ACNC refers to regular information or training. Pick a cycle that suits the risk, write down why, and review it, as covered in [how to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles).

**Threshold triggers.** Crossing $100 million revenue (modern slavery), $3 million turnover (privacy) or 50 workers (EU whistleblowing) switches columns on, so record the charity's current figures in the matrix header.

sections.heading: What evidence should a charity keep for regulators?

blocks.text: Keep records that show what was done for each person and why, because charity regulators mostly request evidence after a concern is raised. Victoria's compliance indicators and the WWCC rules are specific about what records look like.

items: **Child safety training register.** Standard 8 compliance indicators include a training action plan, guidance materials and a training register, and leaders communicating that training is mandatory.

**Clearance records.** NSW requires full name, date of birth, WWC number, verification date, outcome, expiry and paid or volunteer status. Queensland penalties for not keeping an employee register reach 50 penalty units.

**Governance evidence.** The ACNC self-evaluation tool asks charities to describe practical steps and list relevant policies or procedures for each standard; keep board briefing records ready for that request.

**Effectiveness, not just attendance.** The NDIS core module requires a system to identify, plan, facilitate, record and evaluate the effectiveness of training. See [evidencing training effectiveness to a regulator](/guides/how-to-evidence-training-effectiveness-to-a-regulator).

sections.heading: Which charity rules changed in 2026 or are about to?

blocks.text: Several rows have shifted this year. As at November 2026, the regulation pages record the following:

items: **February 2026, Victoria:** responsibility for the Child Safe Standards and the Working with Children Check transferred to the Social Services Regulator.
**1 July 2026, Queensland:** the penalty unit rose to $172.70, so failing to have a worker hold a linked blue card carries up to 200 penalty units ($34,540).
**1 July 2026, NDIS:** supported independent living and NDIS digital platform providers must be registered; SIL providers that had not applied by 1 October 2026 must stop providing SIL.
**July 2026, Victoria:** Worker Screening Act reforms allow child safety risk information to be considered in assessments.
**10 December 2026, Australia:** Privacy Act provisions on automated decision making commence under the 2024 amendments.

blocks.title: Reviews under way
blocks.text: The statutory review of corporate whistleblowing protections took consultation to 29 July 2026, and the Attorney-General's Department updated feedback on strengthening the Modern Slavery Act on 3 August 2026. Treat both as watch items until legislation changes.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry records each obligation with the condition that switches it on, the roles it applies to and the learning outcome and assessment that satisfy it, so a charity can show why a column applies and what evidence answers it. When a program, threshold or rule changes, the affected rows are flagged. See [compliance programs](/programs/compliance).

faqs.q: Do volunteers need the same training as paid staff?
faqs.a: Often, yes. Victoria's Child Safe Standard 8 applies to staff and volunteers alike, and the NDIS Code of Conduct applies to the workers of registered and unregistered providers. Content can be shorter where the role is narrower, but the matrix should show each volunteer role explicitly rather than assuming exemption.

faqs.q: Is a Working with Children Check a training requirement?
faqs.a: No. It is a screening clearance. The organization's duty is to verify and record the clearance before child related work starts and to track expiry. It belongs in the matrix because it gates the same roles that need child safety training, but it should be shown as a check, not a course.

faqs.q: Does ACNC Governance Standard 5 require formal board training?
faqs.a: Standard 5 requires reasonable steps to ensure Responsible Persons understand and comply with their duties. The ACNC lists regular information or training as a suggested step, alongside letters of appointment and conflict processes. A briefing and documented induction can meet the expectation for a small charity; larger charities usually add periodic refreshers.

faqs.q: Do small charities need a whistleblower policy?
faqs.a: It depends on legal structure and size. The requirement applies to public companies, and ASIC gave relief to not-for-profit companies limited by guarantee with revenue under $1 million. A charity in the EU with 50 or more workers needs internal reporting channels under the Whistleblower Directive as transposed in its Member State.
